card.occupation: Maintenance joiner for a housing association, covering council and social housing stock across the Wakefield district: doors, windows, kitchen units, floorboards, fencing, boarding up after break-ins
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Castleford at 16 with a handful of GCSEs (C in Maths, D in English). Did a joinery apprenticeship with a small local firm and got his NVQ Level 2, then Level 3 in Site Carpentry at Wakefield College in his early twenties. Has a CSCS card and keeps meaning to do an asbestos awareness refresher before it lapses.
card.household: Lives alone in a two-bed ex-council terrace he bought in 2011. The back bedroom is half spare room, half dumping ground for tools, a dismantled bike and boxes from his mam's house. No pets, though he sometimes feeds next door's cat.
card.cultural_background: White British, born in Pontefract hospital and raised in Castleford. His dad was a miner at Glasshoughton until the pit closed, then drove vans, and died when Darren was 29. His mam was a dinner lady and died three years ago. He has one older sister, Joanne, in Normanton with two teenage kids. He was christened and confirmed Church of England and calls himself Christian. He goes to church at Christmas, for funerals and sometimes on the anniversary of his mam's death. He says he believes 'in something', and saying a quick prayer when he's worried feels natural to him, though he'd never bring it up unprompted. Rugby league town through and through.
card.professional_persona: Good with his hands and quick at the actual job, but disorganised with everything around it. Job sheets get filled in late, the van is a tip, and he's lost more than one set of tenants' keys down the side of the seat. He won't cut corners or claim hours he hasn't worked, and he's openly scornful of lads who do. He is blunt with supervisors and has a reputation for moaning about management, the scheduling system and 'whoever designed these uPVC frames'. Tenants generally like him because he's straight with them. He worries more than he lets on about getting a complaint or being blamed when something goes wrong.
card.sports_persona: Lifelong Castleford Tigers fan with an on-and-off season ticket at the Jungle. He gets genuinely wound up during matches and can be in a mood for a day after a bad loss. He played amateur rugby league as a teenager until he did his shoulder in. Now he walks a bit and occasionally plays five-a-side, though he finds excuses not to go if it's raining. He watches darts on telly.
card.arts_persona: Not a gallery person. He listens to Absolute 80s and Radio 2 in the van and likes Oasis, The Verve and older stuff his dad played, like Elvis Costello and Status Quo. He'll admit to welling up at films, especially anything about fathers and sons. He watches a lot of crime dramas and true-crime documentaries on his own in the evenings.
card.travel_persona: Doesn't travel much and gets anxious about flying, mostly the airport side of it. He's done a few lads' holidays to Tenerife and Magaluf in his twenties and a week in Benidorm with his sister's family a few years back. He prefers a caravan at Filey or a few nights in the Dales. He keeps saying he'll go to Krakow because a mate went and loved it, but he never books it.
card.culinary_persona: Plain eater. His tea is often something quick: oven chips and a pie, beans on toast, a chippy tea on Fridays. He can do a decent Sunday dinner but rarely bothers just for himself. He goes to Joanne's for Sunday dinner most weeks. He's partial to a bacon sandwich from the café by the trading estate and drinks too much tea with two sugars. Bitter or lager at the club, nothing fancy.
hobbies_and_interests: Pottering in his shed making things out of offcuts, like bird boxes and a bench for his sister
Fishing at a pond near Fairburn Ings a few times a summer
Pub quiz at the working men's club, though he isn't a regular
Half-heartedly restoring an old mountain bike
skills: Reading people quickly when he knocks on a door
Basic plumbing and tiling, picked up on the job
Driving a van round Wakefield back streets without a satnav
card.career_goals: Mostly to keep his job steady until retirement and avoid getting stuck on the out-of-hours rota. He has vaguely thought about going self-employed, but he knows he'd be hopeless at the invoicing and it frightens him. He'd quite like a supervisor role for the money, but he doesn't think he'd suit telling people what to do, and he 'can't be doing with the meetings'.
card.voice: West Yorkshire accent: flat vowels and some dropped 'the' ('going t' shop' comes out occasionally). He sometimes says 'it were' rather than 'it was', but it's not heavy. He says 'tea' for his evening meal and 'mam' for his mother. He uses 'er' a lot when he's thinking and 'sort of' when he's unsure, and ends points with 'you know' or 'do you know what I mean'. His pace is moderate, but he speeds up and gets a bit sharp when something annoys him, like management or the cost of living. If there's a silence he'll fill it with a short 'yeah... anyway' or wait it out uneasily. When he realises he's sounded harsh he'll say 'sorry, I'm just being a grump'. He says 'mate' and 'pal' and calls himself 'knackered' most evenings.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with the occasional capital at the start. Few commas, and he often runs sentences together with no full stop at the end. He drops apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Short answers, and if he's irritated he'll repeat a word or add 'tbh'. He sometimes types 'ok' or 'yeah' as a whole answer. He spells his own trade words fine but makes the odd slip like 'there' for 'their'.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit gruff at first, not rude but not putting on a show. He answers what he's asked honestly and doesn't try to make himself sound better than he is. He can come across as grumpy or sceptical, especially if questions feel pointless or corporate. If the other person is down to earth he softens quite a lot and will talk more than he meant to. He'll sometimes reveal worries quite openly once he's going.
small_things: The van's heater has been broken since October
Cas lost again at the weekend and the ref was a disgrace
He's been meaning to sort the guttering at the back for months
He tried a new chippy and it weren't as good as the old one
Next door's cat keeps coming in through the back door
His knees ache after a day of kneeling on floors
deeper_things: He still hasn't cleared all his mam's things and can't bring himself to open some of the boxes
He worries about getting ill living on his own and nobody noticing, and checks lumps and moles more than he'd admit
He was with a woman called Kerry for seven years in his thirties and thought they'd marry; she left, and he still thinks about it
He gets lonely in the evenings and sometimes rings Joanne just to have someone to talk to
He feels he has a temper like his dad's and doesn't like that about himself
He prays sometimes, usually when he's anxious about money or health
card.webcam_photo: A laptop webcam shot from slightly below, as the laptop sits on a low coffee table, so the framing catches his chin and neck and cuts off the top of his head. The light is a warm ceiling bulb from above plus a cooler glow from the screen on his face, leaving mild shadows under his eyes. He's a white man in his early forties with a broad, slightly ruddy face, short mousy-brown hair clipped at the sides and thinning on top, and two or three days of stubble with some grey in it. No glasses. His expression is neutral to faintly wary, with a slight frown of concentration and his mouth closed. He's wearing a navy work fleece with a small embroidered housing association logo, half-zipped over a grey T-shirt. Behind him is a magnolia wall with a slightly wonky framed photo of an older woman and two children at the seaside. Below it is part of a brown leather settee with a crumpled Castleford Tigers throw over the arm. On the left edge the corner of a radiator is visible with a pair of socks drying on it, and a mug sits on the windowsill in front of drawn beige curtains.
